Topic.label: Common Auxiliary Constructions and Configurations for Congruent Triangles

Question: Given that \(AD\) is a median of \(\triangle ABC\), how can extending the median to twice its length be used to prove \(AB+AC>2AD\)?

Choices.A: Draw a line perpendicular to \(AD\) and prove that two right triangles are congruent
Choices.B: Draw a line through \(D\) parallel to \(AB\) and use the equality of corresponding angles
Choices.C: Take the midpoint \(E\) of \(AB\), join \(DE\), and use the triangle inequality
Choices.D: Extend \(AD\) to \(E\) so that \(DE=AD\), prove \(\triangle ABD\cong\triangle ECD\), and then use the triangle inequality

Solution: Extend \(AD\) to \(E\) so that \(DE=AD\), and join \(CE\). Then \(\triangle ABD\cong\triangle ECD\) (SAS), so \(CE=AB\). In \(\triangle ACE\), \(AC+CE>AE=2AD\), giving \(AB+AC>2AD\).

Original.prompt: 已知 AD 为 △ABC 中线，如何用倍长中线证明 AB+AC>2AD？

choices.text: 作 AD 的垂线，证两个直角三角形全等
过 D 作 AB 的平行线，用同位角相等
取 AB 的中点 E，连接 DE，用三边关系
延长 AD 至 E 使 DE=AD，证 △ABD≌△ECD，再用三边关系

Original.explanation: 延长 AD 至 E 使 DE=AD，连接 CE，则 △ABD≌△ECD（SAS），CE=AB；在 △ACE 中 AC+CE>AE=2AD，即 AB+AC>2AD。
